date.note: arXiv v1 date of the combined analysis of the Phase I and Phase II data.

key_value_text.note: Exponent flattened in the page text ('1031' reads 10^31).
key_value_text.quote: (l) the life time of proton is about 1 x 1031 years, (2) it decays into wide spectrum of decay modes, p -> e+ + pai0, p ->anti-nutrino + K+ and so on
key_value_text.value: Proton lifetime of about 1e31 years, with candidate decays in several modes (p to e+ pi0, p to antineutrino K+); close to SU(5) SUSY GUT predictions (the collaboration's claim, not confirmed by other experiments)

name: Experimental evidence for G.U.T. Proton Decay
notes: The collaboration acknowledges the conflict: "Contrary to this conclusion, as shown in our earlier reports (Ref. 9), our result is that protons are decaying with lifetime of about 10 31 years."

summary.plain: The Kolar group combined 13 years of data and claimed that protons decay with a lifetime of about 10^31 years. Larger detectors such as IMB and Kamiokande set limits near 10^33 years, and no other experiment has confirmed the claim.
summary.technical: Combined Phase I and II analysis (about 13 years, mines closing in 1993): candidate fully contained events interpreted as p to e+ pi0 and p to anti-nu K+ decays with tau_p about 1e31 yr, in disagreement with lower limits of order 1e33 yr from other experiments, which the paper acknowledges; four possible neutron-oscillation events are also reported.

title: Experimental evidence for G.U.T. Proton Decay
why_it_matters: A rare claimed signal of baryon-number violation, from the oldest proton-decay search. Langacker's 1992 review notes that no experiment has observed proton decay and that some candidate events could be neutrino interactions.
